group: bouncer with an irregular defect region
title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0RF_0RD0RA_1RE0LB_1LF0LE_1RC0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0RF_0RD0RA_1RE0LB_1LF0LE_1RC0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Each sweep of the head lengthens a block of the background 1010… at the left end by one cell; behind it, a slowly growing region of defects is rearranged a cell at a time, and nobody has found the rule it follows.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,247 cells have been visited and 22,110 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.528). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: A growing block and a slowly growing defect field
claims.text: At the left-end visits in state F the first block of the 1010… background grows by one per sweep; the number of defects behind it is 16 at 10<sup>5</sup> steps, 21 at 10<sup>6</sup>, 26 at 10<sup>8</sup> and 28 at 10<sup>9</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

facts.text: behind the growing block after 10<sup>9</sup> steps, about logarithmic growth.
No halt in the C simulator; 44,247 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A growing block and a field of defects
html: The tape is the pattern 1010… almost everywhere, interrupted by short defects where two 0s stand together. Each time the head, in state F, is back at the left end, the first block of the pattern is one cell longer than the time before: the head runs across it and then works its way through the defects behind it, zig-zagging a few cells forward and back, moving one or two defects by a cell, before it comes back.

The number of defects grows only about logarithmically (16 after 105 steps, 28 after 109). The blocks right behind the first one wobble by one cell; the later ones change in no pattern found so far. Whether the defect field can ever produce the halting pattern (state A reading a 1) is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.528). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,247 cells (31,864 left of the start, 426 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer whose first block grows by one cell per sweep; behind it a region of defects in the 1010... background, moved one cell at a time by a zig-zagging head, grows about logarithmically and looks irregular.
